G9202.definition: to twist, twirl   or  whirl about  , (Aristophanes Comicus):—; metaphorically   to make dizzy, distract  , (Aeschulus Tragicus): —;Pass.  to whirl about  , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9203.definition:
1.  round, spherical  , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; λίθοι στρ.  pebbles  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2.  circular  , (Plato Philosophus) 
3.  round, compactly formed  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. of ships, στρ. ναῦς, στρ. πλοῖον,  a merchant-  ship,  from its round shape  , as opposite to the long narrow ship-of-war  μακρὰ ναῦς); (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
5.  metaphorically  of phrases,  well-rounded, compact, pithy, terse  , (Aristophanes Comicus):—; adverb , στρογγυλώτατα  as tersely as possible  , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G9207.definition:
1.  the sparrow  , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. ὁ μέγας στρ.  the large bird  , i. e.  the ostrich, Struthio  , (Xenophon Historicus): also called στρουθὸς κατάγαιος (i. e. the bird  that runs on the ground  , does not fly), (Herdotus Historicus); also simply στρουθός, like στρουθοκάμηλος, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9208.definition: the socket   in which the pivot of a door  ὁ στρόφιγξ); moved, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9209.definition:
1.  a turning  , e.g. of a horse, (Xenophon Historicus); ἐν στροφαῖσιν ὀμμάτων with  rolling   of the eyes, (Euripides) 
2.  a twist  , such as wrestlers make to elude their adversary, (Plato Philosophus):—; metaphorically   a trick, dodge  , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3.  the turning   of the Chorus  as they danced from right to left of the   ὀρχήστρα:  the strain sung during this evolution, the strophe  , to which the ἀντιστροφή answers. (ML)

G9210.definition:
1.  the pivot, axle   or  pin on which a body turns  , (Euripides) 
2. στρόφιγγες were  pivots working in sockets  , at top and bottom of a door, which served instead of hinges, (Plutarch) 
3.  metaphorically , στρ. γλώττης, of a  well-hung   tongue, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9212.definition:
1.  anything spread   or  laid out for lying   or  sitting upon, a mattress, bed  , Lat.  stragulum , vestis stragula, (Theognis Elegiacus):—;in  plural   the bedclothes, the coverings of a dinner-couch  , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 
2.  a horsecloth, horse-trappings  , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9213.definition:
a bed spread   or  prepared;   generally,  a bed, couch  , (Pindar), etc.:  a mattress, bedding  , (Xenophon Historicus); στρ. ἄφθιτος, of the golden fleece, (Pindar) 
from στρώτης (ML)

G9214.definition:
1.  hated, abhorred, hateful  , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;with  dative   hateful   or  hostile   to one, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2.  gloomy, sullen  , Lat.  tristis , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὁρᾶν στυγνός  gloomy   to behold, (Xenophon Historicus);—; στυγνὸς εἴκων yielding  sullenly, with an ill grace  , (Sophocles Tragicus);  neuter  as  adverb , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9217.definition: made of the wood of the tree   στύραξ, (Strabo Geographus) (ML)

G9219.definition:
1.  a writing   or  noting down  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2.  that which is written, a writing, book: a history, narrative  , (Thucydides), etc. 
3.  a written contract, a covenant, bond  , Lat.  syngrapha , (Thucydides); συγγ. ναυτικαί  a bond to secure money   lent on bottomry, (Demosthenes Orator); ἀνδριάντα ἐκδεδωκὼς κατὰ συγγραφήν having contracted for its execution, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G9221.definition: set on fire with   or  at once, burn up  , Lat.  comburere , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9224.definition: to mix in with, mingle, blend with  , Χάριτας Μούσαις συγκαταμιγνύς (Euripides):—;Pass.  to be absorbed   in a thing, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9225.definition: to eat up, devour with   or  together  , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9227.definition: to dwell with   one, τινί (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9228.definition:
1. Pass.  to lie together  , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. as Pass. of συντίθημι,  to be composed   or  compounded  , ἔκ τινων of certain parts, (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
3. of written works,  to be composed  , (Thucydides), etc. 
4.  to be contrived, concocted  , (Euripides), etc. 
5.  to be agreed on   by two parties, (Thucydides): in  participle   agreed on, arranged  , αἱ συγκείμεναι ἡμέραι (Herdotus Historicus); κατὰ τὰ συγκείμενα according  to the terms agreed on  , (Herdotus Historicus); ἐκ τῶν ξυγκειμένων (Thucydides) 
6.  impersonal  σύγκειται,  it has been   or  is agreed on  , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; so, συγκειμένου σφι, with  infinitive ,  since   they  had agreed to . .  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9231.definition: to break off  :—;Pass.  to be cramped  , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9235.definition:
1.  called together, summoned  , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. ς. ἐκκλησία at Athens, an assembly  specially summoned   by the στρατηγός (opposite to the ordinary meetings, αἱ κυρίαι); Decret. quoted in (Demosthenes Orator):—;generally, σύγκλητος (i.e. ἐκκλησία);  a legislative body  , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G9238.definition:
1.  to break up, cut up  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2.  to thrash soundly, pound well  , (Xenophon Historicus);—;Pass.,  perfect   infinitive  συγκεκόφθαι (Aristophanes Comicus);  participle  συγκεκομμένος (Euripides) (ML)

G9239.definition: a mixing together, commixture, blending, tempering  , (Thucydides), etc. (ML)

G9241.definition:
1.  a compounding  , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
2.  a comparing, comparison  , (Aristotle Philosopher), etc. (ML)

G9242.definition:
1.  to strike together;   ς. τὼ χεῖρε  to clap   the hands for joy, (Xenophon Historicus); but also  to smite   them  together   in grief, (Lucian):—;Pass.  to be applauded  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2.  to hammer   or  weld together  , (Aristophanes Comicus): hence,  to weld   a number of men into one body, i. e.  organise   them, (Demosthenes Orator), etc.:—; perfect   passive   participle  συγκεκροτημένος  well-trained, in good discipline  , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9243.definition:
1.  to come together by chance  , (Iliad by Homer):  to meet with   an accident, συγκύρσαι τύχῃ (Sophocles Tragicus); εἰς ἓν μοίρας ξυνέκυρσας  art involved   in one and the same fate, (Euripides) 
2. with  participle , like τυγχάνω, συνεκύρησε παραπεσοῦσα νηῦς fell in the way  by chance  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. of events and accidents, like συμβαίνω,  to happen, occur  , (Herdotus Historicus): —; impersonal , with  infinitive , συνεκύρησε γενέσθαι  it came to pass   that . ., (Herdotus Historicus):—;so, in Pass., τὸ ἐς Λακεδαιμονίους συγκεκυρημένον (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. of places,  to be contiguous to  , τινί (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G9245.definition: the fruit of the   συκάμινος,  a mulberry  , Lat.  morum , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G9247.definition: a false accuser, slanderer  , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.; (never used in the modern sense of  sycophant  , i. e. κόλαξ); generally,  a false adviser  , (Demosthenes Orator) (Commonly derived from σῦκον, φαίνω,  one who informed against persons exporting figs   from Attica: better perhaps  a fig-shewer  , i. e.  one who brings figs to light by shaking the tree   (the figs having been hidden in the thick foliage); and then,  metaphorically ,  one who makes rich men yield up their fruit by false accusations).   (ML)

G9248.definition:
1.  false accusation, slander, calumny  , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 
2.  a sophism  , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G9249.definition:
1.  a taking together: a seizing, arresting  , ποιεῖσθαι ξύλληψιν  to arrest  , (Thucydides) 
2.  conception  , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9250.definition:
1.  a gathering, collecting  , (Thucydides):  metaphorically , ἐν γενείου ξυλλογῇ τριχώματος in  the first harvest   of a beard, i. e. in early manhood, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2.  a levying   of soldiers, Lat.  conscriptio , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3.  a summary, recapitulation  , (Demosthenes Orator) 
4. (from Pass.)  an assembly, meeting  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9251.definition:
1.  computation  , (Plato Philosophus) 
2.  a conclusion, inference from premisses  , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9257.definition:
1.  a coming together, meeting, joining  , (Xenophon Historicus):  the juncture   of two parts,  the end  , Lat.  commissura , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. in hostile sense,  an encounter, engagement, battle  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. = συμβόλαιον II,  a contract, covenant  , (Aristotle Philosopher); in (Aristophanes Comicus) Ach. there is a play on signfs. II and III,  encounter   and  accounts, charge   and  charges.   
4. in  plural , συμβολαί were  contributions   for a common meal, πίνειν ἀπὸ συμβολῶν, like  de symbolis(Terentius Grammaticus Latinus) entertainment   itself,  a picnic  , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9259.definition:
1.  a sign   or  token by which one infers   a thing, [  variant  dates Tragica Adespota  ; λαμπάδος τὸ σύμβολον  the token   of the beacon-fire, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;often in  plural , of  marks   on the body, (Euripides); of  omens  , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2.  a pledge   or  pawn  , on which money was advanced, (Lysias Orator) 
3. in  plural   tallies  , Lat.  tesserae hospitales , i.e.  the halves   of a bone or coin, which two persons broke between them, each keeping one piece, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
4. at Athens,  a ticket, counter  , Lat.  tessera , such as were given to the dicasts, on presenting which they received their fee, (Demosthenes Orator) 
5.  a permit   or  licence to reside, given to aliens  , (Aristophanes Comicus);  a ticket   given by each person who joined in a picnic, to be presented for payment at the end (compare συμβολή IV), (Aristophanes Comicus) 
6. in Eccl.  the distinctive mark   of Christians,  a confession of faith, a creed  , Lat.  symbolum . 
7. in legal phrase, σύμβολα were  covenants between two states for protection of commerce  , (Demosthenes Orator), etc.; σύμβολα ποιεῖσθαι πρὸς πόλιν to make  a commercial treaty   with a state, τὰ ς. συγχέειν to violate  such treaty  , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G9261.definition: advice   or  counsel given  , (Herdotus Historicus); in  plural   counsels  , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9262.definition: to be an ally, to be in alliance  , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;generally,  to help, aid, succour  , τινί (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.:—;Pass.  to be assisted  , (Lucian) (ML)

G9263.definition:
1.  an alliance offensive and defensive   (opposite to an ἐπιμαχία,  defensive)  , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: συμμαχίαν ποιεῖσθαι πρός τινα (Herdotus Historicus); τινί (Thucydides) 
2. generally,  the duty of an ally  , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. = τὸ συμμαχικόν,  the body of allies  , (Herdotus Historicus): also,  the country of one's allies  , (Thucydides) 
4.  an allied   or  auxiliary force  , (Thucydides) (ML)

G9264.definition:
1.  commensurate with   another thing, (Euripides):  exactly fitting  , (Aeschulus Tragicus); τῷδε τἀνδρὶ ξ.  being of like age with  , (Sophocles Tragicus); ποίᾳ σύμμετρος τύχ;  coincident with   what chance? i. e. in the very nick of time, (Sophocles Tragicus); see. infr. III. 2. 
2.  commensurable  , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
3.  in measure with, proportionable, exactly suitable  , (Isocrates Orator), etc. 
4.  absolute   in right measure, in due proportion, symmetrical  , opposite to ὑπερβάλλων and ἐλλείπων, (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
5. generally,  fitting, meet, due  , (Aeschulus Tragicus);—; σύμμετρος ὡς κλύειν  within fit distance   for hearing, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
6.  adverb  -τρως, (Isocrates Orator), etc. 
7.  in due time  , (Euripides) (ML)

G9265.definition:
1.  commingled, promiscuous  , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. 
2. with  dative   commingled with  , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9266.definition:
1.  to mix together, commingle  , (Homeric Hymns);  to mix   one thing  with   another, τί τινι (Herdotus Historicus), attic; with  accusative  only, συμμίξαντες τὰ στρατόπεδα  having combined   them, (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., of a river,  to be mingled with   another river, with  dative , (Iliad by Homer):  to join forces  , of two armies, (Thucydides):—; metaphorically , οὐδείς [ ἐστι] τῷ κακὸν οὐ συνεμίχθη there is none who  has not   misery  as an ingredient in his nature  , (Herdotus Historicus); συμμιγέντων τούτων πάντων when all these things  happened together  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2.  to unite  , θεοὺς γυναιξί (Homeric Hymns):—;Pass.  to have intercourse with  , with  dative , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3.  metaphorically , ς. τινὰ τύχᾳ  to make   him  acquainted with   fortune, (Pindar); πρῆγμα συμμῖξαί τινι  to communicate   a matter to another, (Herdotus Historicus) 
4.  intransitive  in Act.  to have intercourse with, to associate   or  communicate with   others, with  dative , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc.; ς. πρός τινα  to join   him, (Xenophon Historicus):—;generally,  to meet for conversation   or  traffic  , (Herdotus Historicus); ς. τινί  to converse with  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
5. in hostile sense,  to meet in close fight, come to blows, engage  , τινί with one, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
6. generally,  to meet  , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9267.definition: commingled, promiscuous  , (Hesiod): especially of troops,  irregular  , (Herdotus Historicus)  adverb  -τως, (Strabo Geographus) (ML)

G9268.definition:
1.  commixture  , τινος πρός τι (Plato Philosophus) 
2.  intercourse  , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9269.definition:
1.  to place beside one also  , (Pindar) 
2. Pass., with  aorist2   et  perfect   active ,  to stand beside, assist  , τινι (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9270.definition:
1.  all together, all at once, all in a body  , (Homer), attic; in attic, the Art. is often added in the case of Numerals, πέντ᾽ ἦσαν οἱ ξύμπαντες (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. with collective nouns,  the whole  , ὁ ς. στρατός (Herdotus Historicus); στρατὸς ς. (Sophocles Tragicus); ξύμπασα πόλις the state  as a whole  , (Thucydides); ξ. γνώμη the  general   scope (of a speech), (Thucydides) 
3. τὸ σύμπαν  the whole together, the sum   of the matter, (Herdotus Historicus); τὸ ξύμπαν εἰπεῖν (Thucydides) 
4. τὸ σύμπαν, as  adverb   altogether, on the whole, in general  , (Thucydides), etc. (ML)

G9271.definition: to tread together, trample under foot  , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor):—;Pass.  to be trampled under foot  , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G9272.definition:
1.  to join   or  assist in accomplishing  , (Euripides):—;Mid., συμπεραίνεσθαί τινι ἔχθραν  to join fully in   enmity  with   another, (Demosthenes Orator) 
2.  to decide   or  conclude absolutely  , ς. φροντίδα to make up one's mind, (Euripides); κλῇθρα μοχλοῖς ς.  to make   the doors  doubly sure   by bars, (Euripides):—;Pass.  to be quite finished  , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9273.definition:
1.  to carry round along with   or  together  , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. Pass.  to be carried round together  , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. συμπεριφέρεσθαί τινι  to have intercourse with   one, (Polybius Historicus):  to adapt oneself to   circumstances, with  dative , (Aeschines Orator) 
4.  to be well acquainted with   things, (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G9275.definition:
1.  to twine   or  plait together  , (Plato Philosophus); τινί with a thing, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus); συμπλέκοντες τὼ χεῖρε εἰς τοὐπίσω  joining   their hands behind them, (Thucydides) 
2. Pass.  to be twined together, entwined, entangled  , (Euripides); ἴχνη συμπεπλεγμένα tracks  entangled, crossing in different directions  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. of persons wrestling,  to be locked together with   another, with  dative , (Herdotus Historicus): generally,  to be engaged in close fight  , (Demosthenes Orator): of a ship,  to be entangled   with her opponent, (Herdotus Historicus):—;then,  metaphorically   to be entangled in  , τῇ Σκυθῶν ἐρημίᾳ συμπλακῆναι (Aristophanes Comicus); συμπεπλέγμεθα ξένῳ  we are entangled   or  engaged with   him, (Euripides); of war,  to be engaged in  , (Demosthenes Orator) 
4.  intransitive  in Act., = Pass., (Euripides) (ML)

G9277.definition:
1.  to tie the feet together, bind hand and foot  , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Pass.  to be entangled in a net  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2.  metaphorically   to entangle  , Lat.  impedire , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9278.definition: to join in war  , (Thucydides), etc.; τινί  with   one, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9280.definition: to join in escorting  , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ς. τινὰ ναυσίν (Thucydides) (ML)

G9283.definition: a chance, casualty  , (Aristotle Philosopher): in bad sense,  a mishap, mischance  , (Thucydides) (ML)

G9286.definition:
1.  to press   or  pack closely together  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2.  absolute  of troops,  to close their ranks, form in close order  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3.  to block up, close  , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9288.definition: to knead together: beat black and blue  , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus):—;Pass., (Euripides); ψυχὴ συμπέφυρται μετὰ τοῦ κακοῦ (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9290.definition: to sweep away  , of a rapid river, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9291.definition:
1.  to sing with   or  together  , (Aeschines Orator); ς. ᾠδάν (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. generally,  to be in accord with  , τινί (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3.  transitive   to celebrate together  , τινά (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G9292.definition: a mutual agreement, covenant, contract  , (Demosthenes Orator), etc.: in  plural   dealings between men  , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G9297.definition:
1.  to tie   or  bind together, to join together, unite  , ς. χέρα, in sign of friendship, (Euripides); ἰδού, ξύναψον (i.e. τὴν χέρα); (Euripides); but, ς. χεῖρά τινος ἐν βρόχοις  to bind   it  fast  , (Euripides):—; ς. πόδα or ἴχνος τινί to meet him, (Euripides); ς. κῶλον τάφῳ to approach the grave, (Euripides); so, φόνος ς. τινὰ γᾷ (Euripides):—; ξ. βλέφαρα  to close   the eyes, (Euripides); ς. στόμα  to kiss   one, (Euripides):—; ς. κακὰ κακοῖς  to link   misery with misery, (Euripides); but, ς. κακόν τινι  to link   him  with misery  , (Euripides): ς. τινὶ δαῖτα  to give   one a meal, (Euripides):  proverbial , ς. λίνον λίνῳ  to join   thread to thread, i. e. to compare things of the same sort, (Plato Philosophus) 
2.  to connect in thought, to combine  , (Plato Philosophus): ς. μηχανήν  to frame   a plan, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ς. ὄναρ εἴς τινα  to connect   it  with   him,  refer   it  to   him, (Euripides); ξυνῆψε πάντας ἐς μίαν βλάβην  involved   them in one loss, (Euripides) 
3. in hostile sense, ς. εἰς μάχην  to bring   into action, (Herdotus Historicus); ἐλπὶς πόλεις ξυνῆψε  engaged   them  in conflict  , (Euripides) 
4. ς. μάχην  to join   battle, (Herdotus Historicus); τινί with one, (Aeschulus Tragicus); πρός τινα (Thucydides): also (without μάχην);  to engage  , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., νεῖκος συνῆπταί τινι πρός τινα (Herdotus Historicus) 
5. in friendly sense,  to unite  , (Xenophon Historicus): —;Pass., συνάπτεσθαί τινι  to have intercourse with  , [  variant  dates Anthology Palantina   
6. with  accusative  rei, ς. μῦθον, ὅρκους (Euripides); ς.τινὶ γάμους, λέκτρα, κῆδος  to form an alliance by   marriage, (Euripides): ξυνάπτεσθαι κῆδος τῆς θυγατρός  to get one's daughter   married, (Thucydides) 
7.  intransitive : 
8. in local sense,  to border on, lie next to  , (Herdotus Historicus); Τήνῳ συνάπτει Ἄνδρος (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
9. of Time,  to be nigh at hand  , (Pindar); so of events, λύπη ς. τινί (Euripides) 
10.  metaphorically  of thoughts,  to meet together  , (Aristotle Philosopher):—;  to be connected with  , πρός τι (Aristotle Philosopher) 
11. of persons, ς. λόγοισι  to enter into   conversation, (Sophocles Tragicus); so, ἐς λόγους ξ. τινί (Euripides); also, ς. εἰς χορεύματα  to join   in the dance, (Euripides); ς. ἐς χεῖρα γῇ, i. e.  to come close   to land, (Euripides) 
12. τύχα ποδὸς ξυνάπτει μοι, i. e. I have come in good time, (Euripides) 
13. Mid.  to be next to, connected with  , τινι (Xenophon Historicus) 
14.  to take part with   one,  to assist  , τινι (Euripides);  absolute , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
15.  to bring upon oneself  , πληγάς (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G9298.definition: to reckon in, to take into the account, enumerate  , (Isaeus Orator); so in Mid., (Aeschines Orator):—;Pass.  to be counted with others, to be taken into account  , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)
